sections.title: Architecture & operating model
sections.response_text:
Architecture and operating model

Prepared by {auditor_name} ({company}) on {date}.

{system_enclave_name} - Generic (CMMC Level 1 / FCI).

The assessed system follows the fixed AIC Server enclave model:

  • Control plane: sign-in, privileged access, inventory, Current State Compliance, Assessment Binder, disclosures, and Secure Share
  • Managed machines with agents where enrolled (agentless discovery where supported)
  • System Groups for compliance and binder sampling scope
  • Recorded Remote Access / Connect for assigned workstations

Organization fields (legal name, CAGE, system name, MSP) fill this instance. They do not redefine the control plane.

Typical deployments run in cloud infrastructure (AIC-operated or customer tenant). On-premises partner models may apply.

AIC usually does not keep standing login access to customer hosts. Day-to-day work uses product roles, justifications, and evidence citations.

Where to cite evidence

  • Systems / Endpoints inventory and enclave systems list
  • System Groups
  • Current State Compliance findings, Fix-It trail, and auditor-pack ZIP
  • Secure Share citations (titles and ids only - no CUI document bodies)
  • Remote Access / Connect session recordings
  • Crypto custody / runtime-status posture
  • Disclosures presets
  • Offline agent enrollment and elevation channel status where in scope

Hardware-token test fixtures, demo passwords, and seed data are not a production authorization or Met claim.

Security design follows NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5. CMMC packaging does not lower that bar.

What IT / MSP needs to do

  1. Stand up and operate the fixed enclave model (network, System Groups, agents, crypto custody) per the MSP and IT admin SOPs.
  2. Keep Current State Compliance inventory synced. Remediate or disposition open findings. Re-scan before claiming progress.
  3. Maintain elevation and password-recovery evidence on managed identities only (dedicated service identities only — never personal administrator accounts).
  4. Complete Assessment Binder parameters, apply the matching playbook, regenerate compliance-driven sections, and export for assessor drop. Leave Lead Assessor / Quality Reviewer blank.
  5. Collect operator evidence the product cannot auto-prove (policies, diagrams, interviews). Do not invent Met from narrative alone.

What the C3PAO needs to do

  1. Treat this package as organization-side packaging of a fixed-design enclave. Challenge Met claims that lack scan or artifact support.
  2. Sample endpoints and operational drill-downs from Current State Compliance and Systems inventory.
  3. Interview the organization or MSP on the assessment boundary, and on how demonstration fixtures differ from customer production when reviewing a demonstration binder.
  4. Complete Lead Assessor and Quality Reviewer sign-offs in C3PAO tooling (not in organization binder fields).
  5. Issue findings from real gaps. Do not treat demonstration controls or hardware-token fixtures as production-ready posture.
